t.pt: Compostos: como o tailandês junta palavras
t.en: Compounds: how Thai puts words together

e.pt: Um composto tailandês se explica pelas regras normais de sintaxe: se você perguntar a um nativo, ele dá uma 'derivação' que faz o sentido aparecer. Em inglês é o mesmo: pergunte o que é 'parking permit' e você ouve 'a permit for parking your car'. A sintaxe da explicação não é a do composto, mas o parentesco de sentido existe. Por isso, quando um composto não fizer sentido, pergunte a derivação a um professor. Se você inventar compostos, tenha sucesso limitado em mente e confira com um nativo antes de usar.
e.en: A Thai compound can be explained by the regular syntax of the language: ask a native speaker and you get a derivation that makes the meaning clear, just as 'parking permit' yields 'a permit for parking your car'. The syntax of the derivation differs from the compound. If you coin your own compounds, check them with a native speaker first.

e.pt: O tipo mais comum soma dois substantivos: สถาน ('lugar') + ทูต ('embaixador') = สถานทูต ('embaixada'); ทหาร ('pessoa militar') + บก ('terra'), เรือ ('barco'), อากาศ ('ar') = soldado, marinheiro, aviador; กระทรวง ('ministério') + การต่างประเทศ = Ministério das Relações Exteriores; กรม ('departamento') + ตำรวจ = Departamento de Polícia; กองทัพ ('forças armadas') + บก/เรือ/อากาศ = Exército, Marinha, Força Aérea. A parte da direita costuma dizer de que tipo é a da esquerda — o contrário do nosso 'de'.
e.en: Noun + noun: สถาน 'place' + ทูต 'ambassador' = 'embassy'; ทหาร + บก/เรือ/อากาศ = soldier/sailor/airman; กระทรวง + การต่างประเทศ; กรม + ตำรวจ; กองทัพ + บก/เรือ/อากาศ. The right-hand element usually tells what kind the left-hand one is.

t.pt: ผู้ e นัก fazem substantivos de agente
t.en: ผู้ and นัก build agent nouns

e.pt: ผู้ entra antes de muitos verbos para formar o 'quem faz', como o nosso sufixo -eiro ou -dor: ผู้ + เชี่ยวชาญ ('ser experiente') = ผู้เชี่ยวชาญ ('especialista'). Ele raramente aparece sozinho. นัก faz o mesmo para um grupo menor e não existe sem o verbo: นัก + ศึกษา = estudante universitário, นัก + เขียน = autor, นัก + ดนตรี = músico. Já ชาวนา, ชาวไร่ e ชาวสวน usam ชาว ('morador de') para lavrador, agricultor e pomareiro.
e.en: ผู้ precedes many verbs to form agent nouns (like English -er): ผู้ + เชี่ยวชาญ = 'expert'; it rarely occurs alone. นัก does the same for a limited set and never stands alone: นักศึกษา 'university student', นักเขียน 'author', นักดนตรี 'musician'.

notas.ex: นัก|nák ศึกษา|sʉ̀k-sǎa

t.pt: Composto ocupa o lugar de um substantivo só
t.en: A compound fills the slot of a single noun

e.pt: Um composto se comporta exatamente como um substantivo simples dentro de outra construção: em เจ้าหน้าตำรวจคนนี้ ('este policial') e นักศึกษาสี่คนนั้น ('aqueles quatro estudantes'), o composto aceita determinante e número + classificador do mesmo jeito. Na prática, isso quer dizer que não é preciso tratar 'สถานทูต' como algo especial: vale tudo o que vale para 'บ้าน'.
e.en: Noun compounds take the same position as single nouns in larger constructions: เจ้าหน้าตำรวจคนนี้ 'this police official', นักศึกษาสี่คนนั้น 'those four students' — they accept determiners and number + classifier just like a simple noun.

notas.ex: นักศึกษา|nák-sʉ̀k-sǎa สี่|sìi คน|kon นั้น|nân

t.pt: อยู่ vem seguido de lugar
t.en: อยู่ is followed by a place

e.pt: อยู่ ('estar situado, morar') pede uma expressão de lugar logo depois: ยูโซมอยู่ที่ถนนเพชรบุรี ('a USOM fica na rua Phetburi'). É a resposta padrão para อยู่ที่ไหนครับ ('onde fica?'), e a resposta começa repetindo o อยู่ — อยู่ที่ถนนสาทรใต้ครับ. Pense no nosso 'fica na rua tal'.
e.en: อยู่ 'to be located at, to live at' is normally followed by a place expression: อยู่ที่บ้าน 'at home', อยู่ที่ถนนเพชรบุรี 'on Petburi Street'. The answer to อยู่ที่ไหน repeats อยู่: อยู่ที่ถนนสาทรใต้ครับ.

notas.ex: อยู่|yùu ที่|tîi ถนน|tà-nǒn สาทร|sǎa-tɔɔn

t.pt: Duas respostas para 'o que você faz?'
t.en: Two answers to 'what do you do?'

e.pt: คุณทำงานอะไร ('o que você faz?') aceita duas respostas. Uma diz o cargo, com เป็น: ผมเป็นเจ้าหน้าที่ ('sou funcionário'). A outra diz o lugar, com ทำงานที่: ผมทำงานที่สถานทูตอเมริกัน ('trabalho na Embaixada Americana'). As duas são completas; a diferença é só o que você quer destacar, o título ou o endereço.
e.en: คุณทำงานอะไร can be answered either with the position — ผมเป็นเจ้าหน้าที่ — or with the place of work — ผมทำงานที่สถานทูตอเมริกัน. Both are complete sentences.

notas.ex: ผม|pǒm ทำงาน|tam-ngaan ที่|tîi สถานทูต|sà-tǎan-tûut

t.pt: ไปไหน × ไปที่ไหน
t.en: ไปไหน vs. ไปที่ไหน

e.pt: As duas perguntam 'aonde você vai?', mas o contexto muda. ไปไหน é a pergunta solta do dia a dia, respondida com a atividade: ไปทานข้าว ('vou comer'). ไปที่ไหน quer o endereço, e a resposta é um lugar: (ที่)ร้านอาหารศรแดง ('no restaurante Red Arrow'). Use ไปที่ไหน quando precisar fixar o ponto no mapa.
e.en: Both mean 'where are you going?', but ไปไหน is the casual question answered with an activity (ไปทานข้าว), while ไปที่ไหน asks for the specific place and is answered with one: (ที่)ร้านอาหาร...

t.pt: ไปไหน? responde-se com a atividade
t.en: Answering ไปไหน with an activity

e.pt: Quando alguém pergunta ไปไหนครับ no portão, a resposta natural é o que você vai fazer, não o endereço: ไปทานข้าวครับ ('vou comer'). Se quiserem o lugar, vem a pergunta de follow-up ไปทานที่ไหนครับ, e aí sim você responde com o restaurante. É o mesmo encadeamento do nosso 'aonde vai?' → 'almoçar fora' → 'onde?'.
e.en: The natural answer to ไปไหน is the activity (ไปทานข้าว 'going to eat'); the place is given only if a follow-up question asks ไปทานที่ไหน.

notas.ex: ไป|bpai ทาน|taan ข้าว|kâao
